hotspots.title: Trump’s explosive NBC interview meltdown
hotspots.blurb: President Trump abruptly ended a live NBC interview after clashing with host Kristen Welker over his claims of election fraud and a blocked $1.8B 'anti-weaponization' fund. The incident sparked widespread media coverage and social media reactions.
hotspots.affect: The interview's abrupt end and Trump's accusations of bias amplified existing grievances among his supporters, reinforcing perceptions of media hostility and government overreach.

hotspots.title: AfD’s surge in German regional elections
hotspots.blurb: The Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) continues to dominate polls in Saxony-Anhalt and other German states, with internal debates over extremism vs. moderation and court victories against left-wing critics. The party's rise is fueled by voter discontent and perceived failures of mainstream parties.
hotspots.affect: The AfD's growing influence has sparked alarm among mainstream parties and civil society, with intense debates over its extremist ties and the effectiveness of Germany's 'firewall' policy against it.

hotspots.title: Patricia Bullrich’s rebellion against Milei
hotspots.blurb: Argentine Security Minister Patricia Bullrich publicly defied President Javier Milei by abstaining from a Senate vote on judicial appointments, exposing deep internal divisions within La Libertad Avanza. The rift has raised questions about the government's stability and future electoral strategy.
hotspots.affect: Bullrich's defiance has intensified internal power struggles within the ruling coalition, with fears of a broader fracture ahead of the 2027 elections.

hotspots.title: Hungary’s EU migration pact protests
hotspots.blurb: Hungarian Prime Minister Péter Magyar faces protests over his government's decision to comply with the EU's migration pact, despite earlier promises to reject it. The move has sparked outrage among nationalist groups and opposition parties, who accuse Magyar of betraying Hungary's sovereignty.
hotspots.affect: The protests reflect deep-seated nationalist grievances and fears of losing control over migration policy, with accusations of government betrayal amplifying the emotional charge.

hotspots.title: Vannacci’s Futuro Nazionale gains momentum
hotspots.blurb: Roberto Vannacci, a far-right Italian general, has launched Futuro Nazionale, a new political party that is rapidly gaining support at the expense of Matteo Salvini’s Lega. The party’s rise threatens to reshape Italy’s right-wing political landscape ahead of the next elections.
hotspots.affect: Vannacci's party is tapping into voter discontent with traditional right-wing parties, with its rapid growth sparking fears of further fragmentation and extremism in Italian politics.
